:::{#rem-indicator-vector-weighted-sums}
#### Indicator vectors build every vector

For $p = 3$, the indicator vectors are
$\vecf{e}_1 = (1, 0, 0)$, $\vecf{e}_2 = (0, 1, 0)$, and $\vecf{e}_3 = (0, 0, 1)$.
Every vector of length $3$ is a weighted sum
$c_1\vecf{e}_1 + c_2\vecf{e}_2 + c_3\vecf{e}_3$ of them,
with weights equal to its entries;
for example,
$(2, -1, 5) = 2\vecf{e}_1 - 1\vecf{e}_2 + 5\vecf{e}_3$.
The weights are unique, since they must be the entries.
Because every vector is a weighted sum of them in exactly one way,
the indicator vectors are also called the standard basis vectors.

:::
